<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
  xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/maven-v4_0_0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <parent>
    <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
    <artifactId>auto-parent</artifactId>
    <version>3</version>
  </parent>

  <groupId>com.google.auto.value</groupId>
  <artifactId>auto-value</artifactId>
  <version>1.2-SNAPSHOT</version>
  <name>AutoValue</name>
  <description>
    Immutable value-type code generation for Java 1.6+.
  </description>

  <properties>
    <guava.version>18.0</guava.version>
  </properties>
  <scm>
    <url>http://github.com/google/auto</url>
    <connection>scm:git:git://github.com/google/auto.git</connection>
    <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git</developerConnection>
    <tag>HEAD</tag>
  </scm>

  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-common</artifactId>
      <version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto.service</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-service</artifactId>
      <version>1.0-rc2</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
      <version>${guava.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.ow2.asm</groupId>
      <artifactId>asm</artifactId>
      <version>4.1</version>
    </dependency>
    <!-- test dependencies -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.apache.velocity</groupId>
      <artifactId>velocity</artifactId>
      <version>1.7</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava-testlib</artifactId>
      <version>${guava.version}</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
      <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
      <version>0.6</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>junit</groupId>
      <artifactId>junit</artifactId>
      <version>4.11</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.truth</groupId>
      <artifactId>truth</artifactId>
      <version>0.25</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>

  <build>
    <resources>
      <resource>
        <directory>src/main/java</directory>
      </resource>
    </resources>

        <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.5</version>

        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>

          <addTestClassPath>true</addTestClassPath>
          <cloneProjectsTo>${project.build.directory}/it</cloneProjectsTo>
          <filterProperties>
            <auto.version>${project.version}</auto.version>
          </filterProperties>
          <pomIncludes>
            <pomInclude>*/pom.xml</pomInclude>
          </pomIncludes>
          <streamLogs>true</streamLogs>
        </configuration>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <id>integration-test</id>
            <goals>
              <goal>install</goal>
              <goal>run</goal>
            </goals>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.immutables.tools</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-shade-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>3</version>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <phase>package</phase>
            <goals>

                    <exclude>com.google.auto.value.**</exclude>
                  </excludes>
                </relocation>
              </relocations>
            </configuration>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>

input.content:
# Fixing Maven `tools.jar` Dependency Issues on Java 9+

## Problem

Java projects built with Maven that depend on `com.sun:tools:jar` (the JDK `tools.jar`) fail
on Java 9 and later because `tools.jar` was removed. Its classes were integrated into the
JDK's module system (`java.compiler` and `jdk.compiler` modules).

## Root Cause

In Java 8 and earlier, `tools.jar` lived at `${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar`. Many Maven POMs
declared a system-scoped dependency:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
  <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  <version>${java.version}</version>
  <scope>system</scope>
  <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
</dependency>
```

On Java 9+, this file simply doesn't exist, causing build failures.

## Solution Approaches

### Approach 1: Add a JDK 9+ Profile (Preferred for older projects)

Add a profile to the parent POM that detects Java 9+ and provides an empty/dummy tools.jar path,
or exclude the dependency:

```xml
<profile>
  <id>jdk9-plus</id>
  <activation>
    <jdk>[9,)</jdk>
  </activation>
  <properties>
    <!-- tools.jar not needed on JDK 9+ -->
  </properties>
</profile>
```

### Approach 2: Exclude Transitive `tools.jar` Dependency

In modules that pull in `compile-testing` (which transitively depends on `com.sun:tools`),
add an exclusion:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
  <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
  <version>0.7</version>
  <scope>test</scope>
  <exclusions>
    <exclusion>
      <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
      <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
    </exclusion>
  </exclusions>
</dependency>
```

### Approach 3: Update `compile-testing` Version

Newer versions of `compile-testing` (0.15+) removed the `tools.jar` dependency
and are compatible with Java 9+.

## Key Diagnostics

```bash
# Check Java version
java -version

# Check if tools.jar exists
ls ${JAVA_HOME}/../lib/tools.jar

# Debug Maven dependency resolution
mvn -X dependency:tree 2>&1 | grep tools

# Find where tools.jar is referenced
grep -r "tools\.jar\|com\.sun" --include="pom.xml" .
```

## Notes

- On Java 9+, the classes from `tools.jar` are available via `java.compiler` and
  `jdk.compiler` modules automatically
- The `system` scope in Maven is generally discouraged; modern approaches use
  standard `compile` scope with proper module declarations
- Source/target compatibility level 1.6 may also need updating for Java 11+
  (minimum supported is 1.6 for compilation but with warnings)

# Maven Java Version Compatibility

## Source/Target Version Configuration

Maven compiler plugin configures Java source and target compatibility:

```xml
<plugin>
  <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
  <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
  <configuration>
    <source>1.6</source>
    <target>1.6</target>
  </configuration>
</plugin>
```

## Java 11 Compatibility Notes

- Java 11 can compile source level 1.6 code but with deprecation warnings
- The `--release` flag (Java 9+) is preferred over `-source`/`-target` for cross-compilation
- Some APIs removed in Java 11 may cause compile errors even with `-source 1.6`

## Common Build Issues on Java 11

1. **tools.jar missing**: See `maven-tools-jar-java11.md`
2. **JAXB removed**: `javax.xml.bind` was removed in Java 11
3. **JavaFX removed**: Moved to a separate module
4. **Nashorn deprecated**: JavaScript engine deprecated

## Maven POM Profile Activation by JDK

```xml
<profile>
  <id>jdk11</id>
  <activation>
    <jdk>[11,)</jdk>
  </activation>
  <!-- Configuration specific to JDK 11+ -->
</profile>
```

## Useful Commands

```bash
# Check effective POM to see resolved profiles
mvn help:effective-pom

# Build with verbose output
mvn -X compile

# Skip tests during compilation check
mvn compile -DskipTests

# Fail at end to see all errors
mvn compile --fail-at-end
```

# Standard Git/GNU Diff Format

## Unified Diff Format

The standard unified diff format used by `git diff` and GNU `diffutils`:

```
--- a/path/to/file
+++ b/path/to/file
@@ -start,count +start,count @@
 context line (unchanged)
-removed line
+added line
 context line (unchanged)
```

### Header Lines
- `--- a/path/to/file` - the original file
- `+++ b/path/to/file` - the modified file

### Hunk Header
- `@@ -L,S +L,S @@` where L = starting line number, S = number of lines
- Lines starting with `-` are removed
- Lines starting with `+` are added
- Lines starting with ` ` (space) are context (unchanged)

## Creating a Diff File

```bash
# From git changes
git diff > changes.diff

# Between two files
diff -u original.txt modified.txt > changes.diff

# Between directories
diff -ru original_dir/ modified_dir/ > changes.diff
```

## Applying a Diff File

```bash
# Apply with git
git apply patch.diff

# Apply with patch command
patch -p1 < patch.diff

# Dry run (test without applying)
git apply --check patch.diff
patch -p1 --dry-run < patch.diff

# Apply in reverse
git apply -R patch.diff
```

## Key Flags

- `-p1`: Strip the first path component (removes `a/` and `b/` prefixes)
- `--check`: Verify the patch can be applied without actually applying
- `-R` or `--reverse`: Reverse-apply a patch
- `--stat`: Show statistics about the patch

## Example Diff

```diff
--- a/pom.xml
+++ b/pom.xml
@@ -40,6 +40,12 @@
   <dependencies>
     <dependency>
       <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
+    </dependency>
+    <dependency>
+      <groupId>com.example</groupId>
+      <artifactId>new-dep</artifactId>
+      <version>1.0</version>
     </dependency>
   </dependencies>
```

# Maven Multi-Module Build Debugging

## Structure

Multi-module Maven projects have a parent POM and child module POMs:

```
project/
├── pom.xml          (parent POM, packaging=pom)
├── module-a/
│   └── pom.xml      (child POM)
├── module-b/
│   └── pom.xml      (child POM)
└── build-pom.xml    (optional convenience POM)
```

## Build Commands

```bash
# Build all modules
mvn compile

# Build specific module
mvn compile -pl module-a

# Build module and its dependencies
mvn compile -pl module-b -am

# Resume from a failed module
mvn compile -rf :module-b

# Build with a specific POM file
mvn -f build-pom.xml compile
```

## Common Issues

### Dependency Resolution
- Child modules inherit from parent POM
- Published parent POMs from Maven Central may differ from local versions
- Use `mvn help:effective-pom` to see the fully resolved POM

### Reactor Build Order

# Fixing Maven `tools.jar` Dependency Issues on Java 9+

## Problem

Java projects built with Maven that depend on `com.sun:tools:jar` (the JDK `tools.jar`) fail
on Java 9 and later because `tools.jar` was removed. Its classes were integrated into the
JDK's module system (`java.compiler` and `jdk.compiler` modules).

## Root Cause

In Java 8 and earlier, `tools.jar` lived at `${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar`. Many Maven POMs
declared a system-scoped dependency:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
  <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  <version>${java.version}</version>
  <scope>system</scope>
  <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
</dependency>
```

On Java 9+, this file simply doesn't exist, causing build failures.

## Solution Approaches

### Approach 1: Add a JDK 9+ Profile (Preferred for older projects)

Add a profile to the parent POM that detects Java 9+ and provides an empty/dummy tools.jar path,
or exclude the dependency:

```xml
<profile>
  <id>jdk9-plus</id>
  <activation>
    <jdk>[9,)</jdk>
  </activation>
  <properties>
    <!-- tools.jar not needed on JDK 9+ -->
  </properties>
</profile>
```

### Approach 2: Exclude Transitive `tools.jar` Dependency

In modules that pull in `compile-testing` (which transitively depends on `com.sun:tools`),
add an exclusion:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
  <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
  <version>0.7</version>
  <scope>test</scope>
  <exclusions>
    <exclusion>
      <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
      <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
    </exclusion>
  </exclusions>
</dependency>
```

### Approach 3: Update `compile-testing` Version

Newer versions of `compile-testing` (0.15+) removed the `tools.jar` dependency
and are compatible with Java 9+.

## Key Diagnostics

```bash
# Check Java version
java -version

# Check if tools.jar exists
ls ${JAVA_HOME}/../lib/tools.jar

# Debug Maven dependency resolution
mvn -X dependency:tree 2>&1 | grep tools

# Find where tools.jar is referenced
grep -r "tools\.jar\|com\.sun" --include="pom.xml" .
```

## Notes

- On Java 9+, the classes from `tools.jar` are available via `java.compiler` and
  `jdk.compiler` modules automatically
- The `system` scope in Maven is generally discouraged; modern approaches use
  standard `compile` scope with proper module declarations
- Source/target compatibility level 1.6 may also need updating for Java 11+
  (minimum supported is 1.6 for compilation but with warnings)

# Maven Java Version Compatibility

## Source/Target Version Configuration

Maven compiler plugin configures Java source and target compatibility:

```xml
<plugin>
  <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
  <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
  <configuration>
    <source>1.6</source>
    <target>1.6</target>
  </configuration>
</plugin>
```

## Java 11 Compatibility Notes

- Java 11 can compile source level 1.6 code but with deprecation warnings
- The `--release` flag (Java 9+) is preferred over `-source`/`-target` for cross-compilation
- Some APIs removed in Java 11 may cause compile errors even with `-source 1.6`

## Common Build Issues on Java 11

1. **tools.jar missing**: See `maven-tools-jar-java11.md`
2. **JAXB removed**: `javax.xml.bind` was removed in Java 11
3. **JavaFX removed**: Moved to a separate module
4. **Nashorn deprecated**: JavaScript engine deprecated

## Maven POM Profile Activation by JDK

```xml
<profile>
  <id>jdk11</id>
  <activation>
    <jdk>[11,)</jdk>
  </activation>
  <!-- Configuration specific to JDK 11+ -->
</profile>
```

## Useful Commands

```bash
# Check effective POM to see resolved profiles
mvn help:effective-pom

# Build with verbose output
mvn -X compile

# Skip tests during compilation check
mvn compile -DskipTests

# Fail at end to see all errors
mvn compile --fail-at-end
```

# Standard Git/GNU Diff Format

## Unified Diff Format

The standard unified diff format used by `git diff` and GNU `diffutils`:

```
--- a/path/to/file
+++ b/path/to/file
@@ -start,count +start,count @@
 context line (unchanged)
-removed line
+added line
 context line (unchanged)
```

### Header Lines
- `--- a/path/to/file` - the original file
- `+++ b/path/to/file` - the modified file

### Hunk Header
- `@@ -L,S +L,S @@` where L = starting line number, S = number of lines
- Lines starting with `-` are removed
- Lines starting with `+` are added
- Lines starting with ` ` (space) are context (unchanged)

## Creating a Diff File

```bash
# From git changes
git diff > changes.diff

# Between two files
diff -u original.txt modified.txt > changes.diff

# Between directories
diff -ru original_dir/ modified_dir/ > changes.diff
```

## Applying a Diff File

```bash
# Apply with git
git apply patch.diff

# Apply with patch command
patch -p1 < patch.diff

# Dry run (test without applying)
git apply --check patch.diff
patch -p1 --dry-run < patch.diff

# Apply in reverse
git apply -R patch.diff
```

## Key Flags

- `-p1`: Strip the first path component (removes `a/` and `b/` prefixes)
- `--check`: Verify the patch can be applied without actually applying
- `-R` or `--reverse`: Reverse-apply a patch
- `--stat`: Show statistics about the patch

## Example Diff

```diff
--- a/pom.xml
+++ b/pom.xml
@@ -40,6 +40,12 @@
   <dependencies>
     <dependency>
       <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
+    </dependency>
+    <dependency>
+      <groupId>com.example</groupId>
+      <artifactId>new-dep</artifactId>
+      <version>1.0</version>
     </dependency>
   </dependencies>
```

# Maven Multi-Module Build Debugging

## Structure

Multi-module Maven projects have a parent POM and child module POMs:

```
project/
├── pom.xml          (parent POM, packaging=pom)
├── module-a/
│   └── pom.xml      (child POM)
├── module-b/
│   └── pom.xml      (child POM)
└── build-pom.xml    (optional convenience POM)
```

## Build Commands

```bash
# Build all modules
mvn compile

# Build specific module
mvn compile -pl module-a

# Build module and its dependencies
mvn compile -pl module-b -am

# Resume from a failed module
mvn compile -rf :module-b

# Build with a specific POM file
mvn -f build-pom.xml compile
```

### Dependency Resolution
- Child modules inherit from parent POM
- Published parent POMs from Maven Central may differ from local versions
- Use `mvn help:effective-pom` to see the fully resolved POM

### Reactor Build Order
- Maven determines build order from inter-module dependencies
- `--fail-at-end` continues building other modules after a failure
- `--fail-fast` (default) stops on first failure

### Parent POM Version Mismatch

  while the local parent POM has a different version (e.g., 4-SNAPSHOT)
- This means changes to the local parent POM won't affect module builds
  unless module POMs are updated to reference the local version

BUILD FAILURE ANALYSIS: google/auto
=====================================

Repository: /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto
Build command (from .travis.yml): mvn -B -U -f build-pom.xml verify --fail-at-end

ERROR SUMMARY
=============

All three compilable modules (common, factory, service) fail with the same error:
  "Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
   /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar"

AutoValue is skipped because it depends on auto-common which fails first.

ROOT CAUSE
==========

The build environment uses Java 11 (OpenJDK 11.0.27), but the project was designed
for Java 7/8. Starting with Java 9, `tools.jar` was removed from the JDK - its
classes were integrated into the JDK's module system (java.compiler, jdk.compiler).

The transitive dependency chain causing the failure:

  Module POM → compile-testing (test scope) → com.sun:tools:jar (system scope)

Specifically:
  - common/pom.xml uses compile-testing 0.7 → depends on com.sun:tools
  - service/pom.xml uses compile-testing 0.6 → depends on com.sun:tools
  - factory/pom.xml uses compile-testing 0.8 → depends on com.sun:tools
  - value/pom.xml uses compile-testing 0.6 → depends on com.sun:tools

The compile-testing library declares a system-scoped dependency:
  <dependency>
    <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
    <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
    <version>${java.version}</version>
    <scope>system</scope>
    <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
  </dependency>

The ${toolsjar} property resolves to ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar, which on
Java 11 evaluates to /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar.
This file does not exist because tools.jar was removed in Java 9+.

ADDITIONAL NOTES
================

- The parent POM (auto-parent version 3, published on Maven Central) and the
  local root pom.xml both define profiles that set the ${toolsjar} property
  based on tools.jar file existence, but neither profile's file-exists activation
  triggers on Java 11 since the file doesn't exist.

- The parent POM's "default-profile" has <activeByDefault>true</activeByDefault>,
  so the ${toolsjar} property is always set even when the file doesn't exist,
  causing the resolution failure.

- Source level 1.6 is supported by javac 11 (with deprecation warnings), so
  no source code changes are needed.

- No Java source files use APIs removed in Java 11 (javax.xml.bind, etc.).

FIX PLAN
========

For each module POM (common, service, factory, value), add an exclusion for
com.sun:tools from the compile-testing dependency:

  <dependency>
    <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
    <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
    <version>...</version>
    <scope>test</scope>
    <exclusions>
      <exclusion>
        <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
        <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
      </exclusion>
    </exclusions>
  </dependency>

This is safe on Java 9+ because the javax.tools API (the reason for the
tools.jar dependency) is available natively in the java.compiler module.

Files to modify:
  1. common/pom.xml   - exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing 0.7
  2. service/pom.xml  - exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing 0.6
  3. factory/pom.xml  - exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing 0.8
  4. value/pom.xml    - exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing 0.6

Good progress - the `tools.jar` issue is fixed. Now there are compilation errors: `javax.annotation.Generated` is not found. This is because `javax.annotation.Generated` was removed in Java 11 (it was in the `java.xml.ws.annotation` module which was deprecated in Java 9 and removed in Java 11). In Java 9+, it was replaced by `javax.annotation.processing.Generated`.

Let me examine the affected files:

There are 3 main source files with compile errors:

1. `factory/src/main/java/com/google/auto/factory/processor/FactoryWriter.java:39` - imports `javax.annotation.Generated`
2. `value/src/main/java/com/google/auto/value/processor/AutoAnnotationProcessor.java:36` - imports `javax.annotation.Generated`
3. `value/src/main/java/com/google/auto/value/processor/AutoValueProcessor.java:51` - imports `javax.annotation.Generated`

In Java 9+, `javax.annotation.Generated` was moved to `javax.annotation.processing.Generated`. Let me look at how these files use the `Generated` annotation to determine the best fix:

Now I need to understand how `Generated` is used in each file. Let me check the usage:

1. **FactoryWriter.java** (line 39, 60, 85): Imports `Generated`, emits it as an import string `"javax.annotation.Generated"`, and uses `Generated.class` in `emitAnnotation`. This is problematic - the `Generated.class` reference requires the import to compile.

2. **AutoAnnotationProcessor.java** (line 36): Imports `Generated` but let me check how it's used.

3. **AutoValueProcessor.java** (line 51): Same.

content.text:
Now I need to understand the approach. The `Generated` class reference is used:

1. **FactoryWriter.java**: Uses `Generated.class` directly in `emitAnnotation`. The fix is to change `javax.annotation.Generated` to `javax.annotation.processing.Generated` (available in Java 9+).

2. **AutoValueProcessor.java**: Uses `Generated.class.getName()` to look up the type element. This processor has logic to handle when `Generated` doesn't exist (as shown in the `GeneratedDoesNotExistTest.java`). Let me look at that code more carefully:

I see now. The AutoValue processor at line 457 uses `Generated.class.getName()` to get the string `"javax.annotation.Generated"` and then looks it up via `getTypeElement`. If it returns null (not found), it gracefully skips it. So the AutoValue code handles the absence of `Generated` already.

The real problem is just the import statement itself - `import javax.annotation.Generated;` causes a compile error on Java 11 because the class doesn't exist.

The fix for all three files is to change `javax.annotation.Generated` to `javax.annotation.processing.Generated`:
- On Java 9+, `javax.annotation.processing.Generated` exists
- `javax.annotation.processing.Generated` has the same `value` attribute

But wait - the FactoryWriter also generates code that emits `"javax.annotation.Generated"` as an import string (line 60). If we change the import in FactoryWriter, the generated factory code would still reference `javax.annotation.Generated`. Let me think about this more carefully.

BUILD FAILURE ANALYSIS: google/auto
=====================================

Repository: /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto
Build command (from .travis.yml): mvn -B -U -f build-pom.xml verify --fail-at-end

ERROR SUMMARY
=============

All three compilable modules (common, factory, service) fail with the same error:
  "Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
   /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar"

AutoValue is skipped because it depends on auto-common which fails first.

ROOT CAUSE
==========

The build environment uses Java 11 (OpenJDK 11.0.27), but the project was designed
for Java 7/8. Starting with Java 9, `tools.jar` was removed from the JDK - its
classes were integrated into the JDK's module system (java.compiler, jdk.compiler).

The transitive dependency chain causing the failure:

  Module POM → compile-testing (test scope) → com.sun:tools:jar (system scope)

Specifically:
  - common/pom.xml uses compile-testing 0.7 → depends on com.sun:tools
  - service/pom.xml uses compile-testing 0.6 → depends on com.sun:tools
  - factory/pom.xml uses compile-testing 0.8 → depends on com.sun:tools
  - value/pom.xml uses compile-testing 0.6 → depends on com.sun:tools

The compile-testing library declares a system-scoped dependency:
  <dependency>
    <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
    <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
    <version>${java.version}</version>
    <scope>system</scope>
    <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
  </dependency>

The ${toolsjar} property resolves to ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar, which on
Java 11 evaluates to /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar.
This file does not exist because tools.jar was removed in Java 9+.

ADDITIONAL NOTES
================

- The parent POM (auto-parent version 3, published on Maven Central) and the
  local root pom.xml both define profiles that set the ${toolsjar} property
  based on tools.jar file existence, but neither profile's file-exists activation
  triggers on Java 11 since the file doesn't exist.

- The parent POM's "default-profile" has <activeByDefault>true</activeByDefault>,
  so the ${toolsjar} property is always set even when the file doesn't exist,
  causing the resolution failure.

- Source level 1.6 is supported by javac 11 (with deprecation warnings), so
  no source code changes are needed.

- No Java source files use APIs removed in Java 11 (javax.xml.bind, etc.).

FIX PLAN
========

For each module POM (common, service, factory, value), add an exclusion for
com.sun:tools from the compile-testing dependency:

  <dependency>
    <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
    <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
    <version>...</version>
    <scope>test</scope>
    <exclusions>
      <exclusion>
        <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
        <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
      </exclusion>
    </exclusions>
  </dependency>

This is safe on Java 9+ because the javax.tools API (the reason for the
tools.jar dependency) is available natively in the java.compiler module.

Files to modify:
  1. common/pom.xml   - exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing 0.7
  2. service/pom.xml  - exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing 0.6
  3. factory/pom.xml  - exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing 0.8
  4. value/pom.xml    - exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing 0.6

BUILD FAILURE ANALYSIS: google/auto
=====================================

Repository: /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto
Build command (from .travis.yml): mvn -B -U -f build-pom.xml verify --fail-at-end

ERROR SUMMARY
=============

All three compilable modules (common, factory, service) fail with the same error:
  "Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
   /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar"

AutoValue is skipped because it depends on auto-common which fails first.

ROOT CAUSE
==========

The build environment uses Java 11 (OpenJDK 11.0.27), but the project was designed
for Java 7/8. Starting with Java 9, `tools.jar` was removed from the JDK - its
classes were integrated into the JDK's module system (java.compiler, jdk.compiler).

The transitive dependency chain causing the failure:

  Module POM → compile-testing (test scope) → com.sun:tools:jar (system scope)

Specifically:
  - common/pom.xml uses compile-testing 0.7 → depends on com.sun:tools
  - service/pom.xml uses compile-testing 0.6 → depends on com.sun:tools
  - factory/pom.xml uses compile-testing 0.8 → depends on com.sun:tools
  - value/pom.xml uses compile-testing 0.6 → depends on com.sun:tools

The compile-testing library declares a system-scoped dependency:
  <dependency>
    <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
    <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
    <version>${java.version}</version>
    <scope>system</scope>
    <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
  </dependency>

The ${toolsjar} property resolves to ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar, which on
Java 11 evaluates to /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar.
This file does not exist because tools.jar was removed in Java 9+.

ADDITIONAL NOTES
================

- The parent POM (auto-parent version 3, published on Maven Central) and the
  local root pom.xml both define profiles that set the ${toolsjar} property
  based on tools.jar file existence, but neither profile's file-exists activation
  triggers on Java 11 since the file doesn't exist.

- The parent POM's "default-profile" has <activeByDefault>true</activeByDefault>,
  so the ${toolsjar} property is always set even when the file doesn't exist,
  causing the resolution failure.

- Source level 1.6 is supported by javac 11 (with deprecation warnings), so
  no source code changes are needed.

- No Java source files use APIs removed in Java 11 (javax.xml.bind, etc.).

FIX PLAN
========

For each module POM (common, service, factory, value), add an exclusion for
com.sun:tools from the compile-testing dependency:

  <dependency>
    <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
    <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
    <version>...</version>
    <scope>test</scope>
    <exclusions>
      <exclusion>
        <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
        <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
      </exclusion>
    </exclusions>
  </dependency>

This is safe on Java 9+ because the javax.tools API (the reason for the
tools.jar dependency) is available natively in the java.compiler module.

Files to modify:
  1. common/pom.xml   - exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing 0.7
  2. service/pom.xml  - exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing 0.6
  3. factory/pom.xml  - exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing 0.8
  4. value/pom.xml    - exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing 0.6
